seo.title: What is a 301 redirect?
seo.description: A 301 redirect is a permanent instruction that a page has moved to a new address, sending both visitors and search engines to it.

definition: A 301 redirect is a permanent instruction that a page has moved to a new address, sending both visitors and search engines to it.
answerBlock: A 301 redirect is a permanent instruction that a page has moved to a new address, sending both visitors and search engines to it. It carries the ranking value of the old address across to the new one. A 302 says the move is temporary and does not.

body.heading: When do you need 301 redirects?
paragraphs: Whenever an address changes: a redesign with a new structure, a replatforming, a merged set of pages, or simply a slug that was edited. Every address that has ever been linked to or ranked needs a destination.

The destination has to be the closest equivalent page. Redirecting everything to the homepage is the classic mistake: it tells a search engine the old page has no equivalent and throws away its value, and it leaves the visitor to start again.
Chains matter. A redirect to a redirect to a redirect wastes crawling effort and slows visitors, so maps are flattened to a single hop.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: The traffic a site has earned over years lives in its addresses. A redesign that drops the redirect map can lose most of it overnight, and rebuilding takes months of work that was already paid for once.
This is why editing a published slug should never be silent: the system should create the permanent redirect automatically, at the moment the change is made.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: On this platform, changing a published slug creates the permanent redirect as part of the change, so an address that has been shared or indexed keeps working.

service.title: Website redesign
service.line: Rebuild a site that stopped working for the business, keep the rankings and pages that earn, and fix conversion, speed or a stalled project on the way.

terms.definition: A/B testing splits live traffic between two versions of a page to see which one produces more of the outcome you care about.
Bounce rate is the share of visits where someone looked at one page and left without doing anything else.
Conversion rate optimisation is the work of increasing the share of visitors who do the thing the page exists for.
